title: Carbon dioxide in three dimensions
hook: Turn a model of CO₂ and examine its shape.

knows: Atoms or cells can be represented with simplified models.
doesNotKnow: The two carbon–oxygen bonding regions lie on opposite sides of carbon. The resulting molecule is linear.

misconception: A familiar diagram automatically reveals the structure or function.
objective: The two carbon–oxygen bonding regions lie on opposite sides of carbon. The resulting molecule is linear.

claims.text: Question, stage and reveal: The two carbon–oxygen bonding regions lie on opposite sides of carbon. The resulting molecule is linear.
The stage is a schematic model and is not drawn to scale.
claims.source: Explicit modelling convention in the stage and reveal.

recall.question: What is the molecular shape of CO₂ around its central atom?
recall.why: The two carbon–oxygen bonding regions lie on opposite sides of carbon. The resulting molecule is linear.
